dedupe_keys.name: the first global multi timescale daily spei dataset from 1982 to 2021

description: The first global multi-timescale daily SPEI dataset from 1982 to 2021 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Xuebang Liu et al. Global warming accelerates water cycle, causing more droughts globally that challenge monitoring and forecasting. The Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) is used to assess drought characteristics and response time of natural and economic systems at various timescales. Coverage: global; published in 2024. Formats: NetCDF. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
